questions.q: Why can a KV cache keep an old token's key and value?
options: Earlier tokens don't change while later ones are generated
Keys and values are the same number
questions.answer: Earlier tokens don't change while later ones are generated
questions.why: A causal decoder's earlier tokens see only what's before them, so their numbers stay fixed.

questions.q: After a cache, what work is left for each new token?
options: Project one token and attend one row against everything stored
Attend all rows, but with fewer heads
questions.answer: Project one token and attend one row against everything stored
questions.why: That is step_cached in the lab.

questions.q: What's the main price of a KV cache?
options: Memory that grows with tokens, layers and key/value heads
questions.answer: Memory that grows with tokens, layers and key/value heads
questions.why: Each layer stores two arrays. The table in the lab sizes them.

questions.q: Why don't ordinary diffusion samplers use a KV cache from step to step?
options: Each step changes every token in the latent, so old keys are stale
questions.answer: Each step changes every token in the latent, so old keys are stale
questions.why: The cache rule needs earlier tokens to stay the same. Sampling changes all of them.

questions.q: You edit an early token and keep the old cache. What happens?
options: The output goes wrong, as the lab shows
The token is ignored and the output is unchanged
questions.answer: The output goes wrong, as the lab shows
questions.why: The lab's stale cache gives an answer far from a full recompute.
